subject: Coordination: security exhibit gating, evidence escrow & pen-test runbook (MSA / Order Form)
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@beaconlabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@beaconlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on security exhibit / pen-test expectations

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — BeaconLabs is excited about the potential. Before procurement and legal escalate to signatures we need to lock down the security exhibit and a few operational details in the Order Form / MSA:

1) SOC 2 evidence cadence — we will need a clear path for requesting artifacts tied to CIAs and for sampling (frequency and sample size).
2) Pen-test language — what notice do you require, and can you support a 3rd-party assessor with scoped discovery and ephemeral staging access?
3) Evidence escrow / temporary access — we need to understand how logs, SOC artifacts, and pen-test reports are delivered and retained.
4) On-call & emergency access — if we find a production-impacting issue during our testing window, what is the on-call escalation and SLA?

I've attached a short spreadsheet (Beacon_Security_Questions.xlsx) that maps our minimum asks to corresponding MSA exhibit clauses — procurement asked for this to be explicit.

Can you propose a concise execution plan (owners, notice windows, evidence handoff steps) so legal can redline in one pass? We are aiming to sign by the end of August.

Appreciate it,

Laura Chen
Head of IT Security
BeaconLabs
[Attachment: Beacon_Security_Questions.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@beaconlabs.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on security exhibit / pen-test expectations

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. Putting a proposed execution playbook below so legal and security have a starting point for redlines. Happy to walk through on a quick call.

High-level playbook (proposed):
- Evidence cadence (SOC 2):
  - Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report on a rolling 12-month basis via secure share (monthly updates to artifact index).
  - For ad-hoc artifact requests (controls evidence), we propose a 10-business-day SLA and a defined sample set (up to 10 artifacts per request) unless urgent (see incident flow).
- Pen-test / inspection windows:
  - Pen-test notice: 30 calendar days preferred; 14 calendar days accepted with elevated approval (for urgent red-teams).
  - Ephemeral staging: we can provision a staging environment for testing; access expires OTP/ephemeral keys.
  - Scoped discovery: assessments limited to agreed systems (Order Form exhibit).
- Evidence escrow & delivery:
  - Final pen-test report and associated logs delivered via encrypted S3 share to your security mailbox; Redwood retains a copy for 90 days for dispute resolution unless otherwise negotiated.
- On-call & escalation:
  - Redwood will name an engineering on-call for test windows; security POC (Karthik) will be on pager for critical/production-impact findings. Response SLA: initial ack within 2 hours, remediation plan within 48 hours.
- Legal controls / gating:
  - We propose inspection to be limited to written notice and bounded samples (no live inspection of other tenants).

Owners & next steps:
- Redwood security owner: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwood.com) — technical clarifications and staging access
- Redwood legal owner: Vanessa Ortiz (vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com) — contract redlines and order form exhibit
- Customer owner: Laura Chen / Amit Rao — acceptance of windows and assessor identity

Timeline suggestion:
- This week: Legal redlines (Vanessa) into a single tracked document
- Next week: customer review and alignment call (propose Aug 20)
- Target: Order Form signed and DocuSign envelope circulated by Aug 25

Attached is an initial exhibit draft for your review (redwood_security_exhibit-draft.pdf). I will loop Vanessa and Karthik to capture legal and technical guardrails.

Thanks — Jonas
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_security_exhibit-draft.pdf (PDF)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@beaconlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordination: security exhibit gating, evidence escrow & pen-test runbook (MSA / Order Form)

Jonas / team — thanks for drafting. I pushed a set of legal-focused redlines and guidance; summary below to make redline review faster for BeaconLabs legal: 

Key legal points to include in exhibit / order form: 
- Scoped inspection clause: inspections limited to specific systems/applications enumerated in the Order Form; no live access to other tenants; sampling only (example: 10% of discrete artifacts or max 10 items per request).
- Notice windows & approvals: standard 30-day notice for routine pen-tests; require mutual signed statement for any 3rd-party assessor and an NDA; customer-provided IP ranges for test be pre-approved.
- Data handling & retention: pen-test reports classified as "sensitive"; Redwood will redact PII and tenant-identifying metadata before sharing where appropriate; retention policy for copies = 90 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Emergency escalation carveout: if a test uncovers an active exploit, Redwood will follow the emergency response runbook and will provide real-time remediation updates; this is not considered a waiver of any SLA or claim.
- Limitation of liability / indemnity alignment: do not accept open-ended access that could expand liability; keep language symmetrical and scope-limited to test window.

I'll attach the Word doc with tracked changes (legal_redlines.docx). Once Beacon confirms they are comfortable with the scope and the assessor, we can consolidate and circulate a single redline set to their counsel. Procurement items (billing, any order-form addenda) should be coordinated once terms are settled.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: legal_redlines.docx (DOCX)]
